summary: Flathead NF L-4 tower built 1937, abandoned 1949; firelookout.com calls the site ruins while the FFLA list marks it gone; no source describes it today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1949; firelookout.com page says ruins, while the FFLA Montana list marks it gone. No source describes the ruins today

evidence.supports: location: 16 miles east of the Spotted Bear ranger station (R.S.), Flathead County, Montana
evidence.quote: 16 miles east of Spotted Bear R.S.

evidence.supports: over 8,000 fire lookouts in 49 states at one time; national inventory completed by the Forest Fire Lookout Association with the U.S. Forest Service
evidence.quote: At one time, there were over 8,000 fire lookouts in 49 states according to the national inventory completed by the Forest Fire Lookout Association in cooperation with the U.S. Forest Service

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA Montana list marks the tower gone; the firelookout.com page says the site is ruins. The story reports both. The record's gone status matches the list.

notes_for_editor: Only two lookout pages plus the FFLOS national count; no staffing, fire, or access source found. Do not confuse with the Pot Mountain Lookout Site on firetower.org, which is in Idaho (URL path us/id); it came up in search and was not used. The firelookout.com page's 'Spotted Bear R.S.' is expanded to 'ranger station' in the story; that reading is not checked against a Forest Service source. The Trails of the Past PDF has no mention of this tower. Ruins versus gone is the open question for a visitor; the story does not resolve it. Elevation is in feet from the source; the record's elevation_m is null. Read budget went over the per-tower guide because sources are thin. WebSearch used twice.
